title: UNIT 2: UNIFORMLY ACCELERATED MOTION
notes:
✓ Motion → Describes a change in position with time.

✓ Uniform motion → Occurs when an object moves with constant velocity.
✓ Accelerated motion → Occurs when velocity changes in magnitude, direction, or both.

◆ UNIFORMLY ACCELERATED MOTION
✓ Uniformly accelerated motion → Motion in which velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, so acceleration remains constant.

◆ Examples
A bicycle slowing down uniformly • an object falling under gravity.

title: 2.1 POSITION AND DISPLACEMENT
notes:
◆ FRAME OF REFERENCE
✓ Frame of reference → An arbitrary set of axes from which the position and motion of an object are described.

◆ POSITION
✓ Position → Location of an object relative to a chosen origin/reference point.

✓ Position → May be positive or negative depending on the chosen reference point.
✓ SI unit → metre (m).

◆ DISTANCE
✓ Distance → Total length of the path travelled by an object from its initial to final position.
✓ Distance → Scalar quantity.
✓ Distance → Always non-negative.
✓ Distance → Depends on the actual path followed.

◆ DISPLACEMENT
✓ Displacement → Difference between the initial and final positions of an object.

Δs = s − s₀

✓ Displacement → Vector quantity.
✓ Displacement → Has magnitude and direction.
✓ Displacement → Represents the shortest directed separation between initial and final positions.

◆ IMPORTANT
✓ Distance ≥ magnitude of displacement.

✓ If an object returns to its starting point → Displacement = 0, but distance travelled is not zero.

title: 2.2 AVERAGE VELOCITY AND INSTANTANEOUS VELOCITY
notes:
◆ VELOCITY
✓ Velocity → Describes how quickly position changes and includes direction.

◆ AVERAGE VELOCITY
✓ Average velocity → Displacement divided by time interval.

vₐᵥ = Δs/Δt = (s − s₀)/(t − t₀)

✓ SI unit → m/s.

◆ AVERAGE SPEED
✓ Average speed → Total distance travelled divided by total time taken.

vₐᵥ = sₜₒₜ/tₜₒₜ

✓ Motion along a straight line in one direction → Magnitude of average velocity equals average speed.

◆ INSTANTANEOUS VELOCITY
✓ Instantaneous velocity → Velocity at a particular instant or over an infinitesimally small time interval.

v = Δs/Δt as Δt → 0

✓ Instantaneous velocity → Gives both the speed and direction of motion at that instant.

◆ SPEEDOMETER
✓ Speedometer reading → Represents the magnitude of a vehicle's instantaneous velocity.

◆ KEY DIFFERENCE
✓ Average velocity → Describes motion over a time interval.
✓ Instantaneous velocity → Describes motion at a particular instant.

title: 2.3 ACCELERATION
notes:
✓ Acceleration → Rate at which velocity changes with time.

◆ AVERAGE ACCELERATION
✓ aₐᵥ = Δv/Δt = (v − v₀)/(t − t₀)

✓ SI unit → m/s².

◆ ACCELERATION OCCURS WHEN AN OBJECT
✓ Speeds up.
✓ Slows down.
✓ Changes direction.

◆ DIRECTION OF ACCELERATION
✓ Acceleration → Points in the direction of the change in velocity.

✓ Velocity and acceleration in the same direction → Speed increases.
✓ Velocity and acceleration in opposite directions → Speed decreases (deceleration).

◆ IMPORTANT
✓ Deceleration → Means the magnitude of velocity is decreasing.

✓ Deceleration → Does not simply mean that acceleration must have a negative numerical value; the sign depends on the chosen positive direction.

◆ INSTANTANEOUS ACCELERATION
✓ Instantaneous acceleration → Acceleration at a particular instant or over an infinitesimally small time interval.

✓ Instantaneous acceleration → Gives the exact rate at which velocity is changing at that instant.

◆ KEY IDEA
✓ Velocity → Tells how quickly position changes.
✓ Acceleration → Tells how quickly velocity changes.

title: 2.4 EQUATIONS OF MOTION WITH CONSTANT ACCELERATION
notes:
✓ Constant-acceleration equations → Relate displacement, initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration and time for motion in a straight line.

◆ BASIC VARIABLES
✓ v₀ → Initial velocity.
✓ v → Final velocity.
✓ s → Displacement.
✓ a → Constant acceleration.
✓ t → Elapsed time.

◆ FINAL VELOCITY
✓ v = v₀ + at

◆ AVERAGE VELOCITY
✓ vₐᵥ = (v₀ + v)/2

◆ DISPLACEMENT
✓ s = vₐᵥt

✓ Therefore:
s = [(v₀ + v)/2]t

◆ DISPLACEMENT USING INITIAL VELOCITY
✓ s = v₀t + ½at²

◆ EQUATION WITHOUT TIME
✓ v² = v₀² + 2as

◆ WHEN TO USE
✓ v = v₀ + at → When displacement is not needed.
✓ s = v₀t + ½at² → When final velocity is not needed.
✓ v² = v₀² + 2as → Useful when time is unknown.
✓ s = [(v₀ + v)/2]t → When both initial and final velocities are known.

◆ SIGN CONVENTION
✓ Choose a positive direction first.
✓ Quantities pointing in the opposite direction → Are assigned negative signs.

title: 2.4 FREE FALL
notes:
✓ Free fall → Motion of an object under the influence of gravity alone, with air resistance neglected.

◆ GRAVITATIONAL ACCELERATION
✓ Acceleration near Earth's surface:
g = 9.80 m/s²

✓ Direction → Downward.

✓ Value of g → Is maximum at Earth's surface, decreases with altitude and varies slightly with latitude.

◆ FREE-FALL EQUATIONS
✓ Replacing a with g and displacement s with vertical height h:

v = v₀ + gt

h = v₀t + ½gt²

v² = v₀² + 2gh

◆ IMPORTANT
✓ In the absence of air resistance → Objects fall with the same gravitational acceleration regardless of their mass.

✓ Object released from rest → v₀ = 0.

✓ Therefore:
v = gt

h = ½gt²

v² = 2gh

title: 2.5 GRAPHICAL REPRESENTATION OF UNIFORMLY ACCELERATED MOTION
notes:
✓ Uniformly accelerated motion → Can be represented using position-time, velocity-time and acceleration-time graphs.

◆ POSITION-TIME (s–t) GRAPH
✓ For constant acceleration:
s = v₀t + ½at²

✓ Position → Depends quadratically on time, so the graph is a parabola.

◆ SLOPE OF s–t GRAPH
✓ Slope of a tangent to the position-time graph → Gives instantaneous velocity.

v = slope of tangent.

◆ VELOCITY-TIME (v–t) GRAPH
✓ For constant acceleration:
v = v₀ + at

✓ Velocity → Varies linearly with time, so the graph is a straight inclined line.

◆ SLOPE
✓ Slope of v–t graph → Acceleration.

a = Δv/Δt

◆ AREA UNDER v–t GRAPH
✓ Area under the velocity-time graph → Displacement.

◆ ACCELERATION-TIME (a–t) GRAPH
✓ Uniformly accelerated motion → Has constant acceleration, so the graph is a horizontal line parallel to the time axis.

◆ AREA UNDER a–t GRAPH
✓ Area under acceleration-time graph → Change in velocity.

Δv = aΔt

◆ GRAPH SUMMARY
✓ s–t tangent slope → Instantaneous velocity.
✓ v–t slope → Acceleration.
✓ v–t area → Displacement.
✓ a–t area → Change in velocity.

title: 2.6 RELATIVE VELOCITY IN ONE DIMENSION
notes:
✓ Motion and velocity → Must always be described relative to a reference frame.

◆ RELATIVE MOTION
✓ Relative motion → The motion observed for an object depends on the observer's frame of reference.

✓ Example → A passenger sitting inside a moving train is at rest relative to another passenger, but is moving relative to an observer standing on the ground.

◆ RELATIVE VELOCITY
✓ Relative velocity → Velocity of one object with respect to another object or observer.

✓ For objects A and B:
v₍AB₎ = vA − vB

v₍BA₎ = vB − vA

◆ SAME DIRECTION
✓ Two objects moving in the same direction → Magnitude of their relative velocity is the difference between their speeds.

|vrel| = |vA − vB|

✓ Example → 100 km/h and 60 km/h in the same direction:
vrel = 40 km/h.

◆ OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS
✓ Two objects moving in opposite directions → Relative speed is the sum of their speeds.

|vrel| = |vA| + |vB|

✓ Example → 100 km/h and 100 km/h in opposite directions:
|vrel| = 200 km/h.

✓ Two objects → Can both be moving relative to the ground but be at rest relative to each other if they have the same velocity.

title: UNIT 2: QUICK REVISION
notes:
◆ POSITION
✓ Location relative to an origin/reference point.

◆ DISTANCE
✓ Total path length; scalar.

◆ DISPLACEMENT
✓ Change in position; vector.

◆ AVERAGE VELOCITY
✓ vₐᵥ = Δs/Δt.

◆ INSTANTANEOUS VELOCITY
✓ Velocity at a particular instant.

◆ AVERAGE ACCELERATION
✓ aₐᵥ = Δv/Δt.

◆ INSTANTANEOUS ACCELERATION
✓ Acceleration at a particular instant.

◆ UNIFORM ACCELERATION
✓ Equal changes in velocity in equal time intervals.

◆ EQUATIONS
✓ v = v₀ + at.
✓ s = v₀t + ½at².
✓ v² = v₀² + 2as.
✓ s = [(v₀ + v)/2]t.

◆ FREE FALL
✓ Motion under gravity alone; g ≈ 9.80 m/s².
✓ v = v₀ + gt.
✓ h = v₀t + ½gt².
✓ v² = v₀² + 2gh.

◆ s–t GRAPH
✓ Parabola; tangent slope = instantaneous velocity.

◆ v–t GRAPH
✓ Straight line; slope = acceleration; area = displacement.

◆ a–t GRAPH
✓ Horizontal line; area = change in velocity.

◆ RELATIVE VELOCITY
✓ vAB = vA − vB.

◆ SAME DIRECTION
✓ Relative speed = difference of speeds.

◆ OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS
✓ Relative speed = sum of speeds.

✓ MASTER IDEA → Uniformly accelerated motion connects position, velocity, acceleration, equations, graphs, free fall and relative motion.
